jobs.description:
Analog IC Design Lead – Power Management

Lotus Microsystems is looking for a motivated and experienced Analog IC Design Lead – Power Management to join our team at our headquarters in Copenhagen. Join a DeepTech company at the forefront of innovation, where ideas move quickly from concept to reality in a collaborative startup environment.

Position Summary

We are looking for an experienced Analog IC Design Lead – Power Management to join our Engineering team. You will lead and contribute to the development of next-generation power converters for a wide range of applications.

You will work on state-of-the-art power management technology alongside a team with hands-on expertise in power electronics, IC design, and semiconductor process development. The role combines technical leadership with hands-on circuit design and close collaboration across disciplines.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide technical leadership for IC development projects and design activities.

• Design integrated power converters and monitoring circuits.

• Design analog and mixed-signal circuit blocks.

• Drive and coordinate IC design and layout activities, working closely with design and layout engineers.

• Simulate and verify circuits using transistor-level and system-level simulation tools.

• Contribute to silicon validation, characterization, and troubleshooting.

• Collaborate with engineers across IC design, power electronics, semiconductor processes, and system development.

Qualifications

• Master’s degree (or higher) in Electrical Engineering or a related field.

• At least 10 years of relevant IC design experience.

• Strong understanding of and hands-on experience with power converters, such as linear regulators, switched-inductor DC-DC converters, and switched-capacitor DC-DC converters.

• In-depth knowledge and hands-on experience in designing integrated power converters, gate drivers, and PWM control circuits.

• In-depth knowledge and hands-on experience in designing analog circuits, including comparators, amplifiers, current sensors, temperature sensors, bandgap references, and related building blocks.

• Experience with IC design environments and EDA tools, such as Cadence (preferred), Synopsys, and/or Mentor Graphics.

• Experience with technical leadership, project leadership, and/or technology leadership in previous IC development projects is a plus.

• Experience with power management ICs (PMICs) and DC-DC converter applications is a plus.

• Experience with PCB design, assembly, and experimental/silicon validation is a plus.

Personal Competencies

• Based in Copenhagen or within reasonable commuting distance. Lotus Microsystems will support relocation for the right candidate, where needed.

• Ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary and international team.

• A creative, curious, and innovative mindset, with a passion for solving complex technical challenges.

• Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain and champion new ideas, actively contribute to brainstorming, and present technical concepts clearly.

• Strong planning and time-management skills, with the ability to adapt to changing priorities in a fast-paced startup environment.

Additional Information

For more information about the position, please contact Martin Lantz, IC Design Manager, at mlantz@lotus-microsystems.com.

We will process candidates on a running basis.

About Us

Lotus Microsystems creates advanced power solutions that transform power and thermal management, unlocking the full potential of AI and advanced computing. Our patented power silicon interposer technology enables miniaturized power delivery systems with exceptional power density and thermal performance.

At Lotus Microsystems in Copenhagen, you will experience an informal, collaborative, and hands-on work environment. Our open office setup fosters strong teamwork and close interaction among colleagues.

Although we are a small team, we are truly international, with colleagues from diverse professional and cultural backgrounds. This diversity enriches our work and gives us a global perspective that resonates with our international customers and partners.

Join Lotus Microsystems and help us develop cutting-edge power technology that can make a meaningful impact on the future of AI and advanced computing.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, the Plant Nutrition Research Group invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in foliar application of nanozymes. The project is part of the research project: “Biocompatible nanozymes with anti-oxidative properties to increase crop resilience in a changing climate”, funded by The Independent Research Fund Denmark.

Start date is expected to be January 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project

As PhD student, you will investigate the mechanisms by which biocompatible Fe-, Mn- and Zn-based nanozymes are taken up, transported and function within plants under drought stress. The work will focus on advanced imaging of nanozyme localization and cellular interactions using LA-ICP-TOF-MS, TEM-EDX and confocal microscopy, combined with analyses of ROS scavenging and oxidative stress responses. You will evaluate how nanozyme treatments influence drought tolerance in climate chamber and field experiments. The project aims to generate fundamental knowledge on nanozyme behaviour in plants and support the development of safe, effective nano-enabled strategies for improving crop resilience to drought.

Who are we looking for?

We are seeking a highly motivated and ambitious PhD candidate with a strong interest in the interface between plant science, nanotechnology and advanced imaging. The candidate should hold a Master's degree in Plant Science, Biology, Agricultural Science, Nanoscience, Biotechnology or a related discipline. The successful candidate will investigate the uptake, transport and intracellular behavior of biocompatible nanozymes in plants exposed to drought stress. It is a clear advantage if you have hands-on experience with LA-ICP-TOF-MS, TEM-EDX and confocal microscopy, as well as knowledge of reactive oxygen species (ROS) dynamics and general plant stress physiology. The candidate should be enthusiastic about interdisciplinary research and willing to work across the fields of plant biology, analytical chemistry and nanotechnology. The candidate is expected to be independent, collaborative and curious, and to contribute actively to an international research environment involving close collaboration between group members.

Our group and research- and what do we offer?

As PhD student in the project, you will join the Plant Nutrition Research Group (www.husted-lab.com) at the University of Copenhagen, an internationally recognized and interdisciplinary research environment working at the interface between plant nutrition, analytical chemistry and nanotechnology. The group conducts both fundamental and applied research aimed at improving nutrient use efficiency, crop resilience and the sustainability of agricultural production systems. We place strong emphasis on maintaining a friendly, collaborative and supportive working atmosphere, where team members openly share knowledge, ideas and expertise. We believe that excellent science is best achieved through dedicated teamwork, mutual respect and a positive working environment that supports both scientific excellence and personal development. As PhD student, you will receive close scientific mentorship, access to world-class infrastructure and the opportunity to contribute to pioneering research addressing some of the major challenges facing future agriculture, including drought resilience, nutrient efficiency and climate adaptation of crops.

Principal supervisor is Professor Søren Husted, Department of plant and Environmental Sciences, Email shu@plen.ku.dk.

********************************************************************************

The PhD programme

A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme

Qualifications needed for the regular programme

To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. plant science, plant nutrition. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

Terms of employment in the regular programme

Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

• Carry through an independent research project under supervision

• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE

• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad

• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities

• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals

• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project

We are looking for the following qualifications:

• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project

• Relevant publications

• Relevant work experience

• Other relevant professional activities

• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in plant science, nanotechnology and advanced imaging

• Good language skills

***************************************************************************

Application and Assessment Procedure

Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

Please include:

• Motivated letter of application (max. one page)

• Your motivation for applying for the specific PhD project

• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position

• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.

• Publication list (if possible)

• Reference letters (if available)

Application deadline:

The deadline for applications is 23 October 2026, 23:59 GMT+2.

We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

The further process

After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in week 45 and 46 2026.

jobs.description:
The Department of Food Science and the Niels Bohr Institute invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in colloidal research in food science. The PhD project has the overall goal of describing the molecular structure of casein micelles through computational and experimental investigations, with focus on the role of κ caseins. The candidate will be part of the CaIFF center for the use of neutrons for the investigation of colloids and interfaces in food science and pharmacy (https://pharmacy.ku.dk/research/caiff/).

Expected start date is 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project

Background. Casein micelles (CMs) are the main protein constituent of milk (80% of protein) and defining for dairy product taste and structure. CMs are 100-200 nm globular particles, formed by a hydrated network of disordered casein proteins, named αS1, αSs, β, and κ casein. The caseins are cross-linked through binding to ionic calcium and colloidal calcium phosphate, and through hydrophobic interactions. Post-translational modifications play an important role in this, as the ionic interactions are largely mediated by casein phosphorylation sites. The CMs are stabilized by κ caseins that are believed to form a hairy layer on the CM surface. Therefore, κ casein are particularly important for CM stability. κ caseins moreover contain a rennet cleavage site, separating its anchoring para κ casein domain from the water-soluble caseinomacropeptide, the primary component of the stabilizing hairy layer. Enzymatic cleavage of this site promotes coagulation and curd formation.

Goal. Despite decades of research, central questions remain regarding the CM structure, their molecular organization, and dynamic behaviour. The goal of the PhD project is to answer fundamental questions like: are all caseins needed for CM formation? What is the role of post-translational modifications in the casein-calcium network formation, and in the κ casein hairy layer? How extended is the stabilizing hairy layer, and how does it depend on for example pH or solvent? What is the dynamic exchange of caseins between soluble caseins or other CMs? In other words, the PhD project’s aim is to understand the molecular interactions in CM which are central to the unique food properties of dairy products like milk, cream, and cheese, with a particular focus of κ casein.

How. Methodological strategy involves state-of-the-art molecular dynamics simulations for building a molecular model of casein micelles. Advanced x-ray and neutron scattering experiments, will be used to validate the model. Scattering experiments provide information of the hierarchical structure of CMs, whereas molecular simulations model the molecules and their interactions. The combination of simulations and scattering data is particularly strong, as the simulated molecular predictions can be validated experimentally. The project thus involves preparing samples, collecting and analysing scattering data and complementary data when needed, and running MD simulations and comparing these to the experimental data. Finally, the candidate needs to posses good written and oral communication skills.

jobs.occupation: Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions
jobs.description:
The University seeks to appoint a tenure track assistant professor to commence 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Information on the department can be found at: https://www.sund.ku.dk/.

Subject area: Infectious disease epidemiology, modelling, animal health, One Health, and sustainable health systems

The Tenure-Track Assistant Professor will lead research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, with particular emphasis on how changes in environmental conditions, animal populations, production systems, and management practices influence disease emergence, transmission, and control. The position will combine infectious disease epidemiology, mathematical and statistical modelling, data science, and economic analysis to generate evidence supporting disease preparedness, prevention, and control.

The successful candidate will:

• Lead independent research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, including the influence of environmental and production system changes.

• Develop and apply simulation, epidemiological, and statistical models to assess disease and spillover risks, evaluate mitigation and control strategies, and quantify their economic implications.

• Demonstrate strong programming skills in R and other relevant programming languages, including experience in managing, processing, and analysing large and complex datasets.

• Have experience in developing and applying epidemiological disease-spread models, including model calibration, validation, parameter estimation, and calculation of epidemiological indicators such as the basic reproduction number (R₀) across different animal species and production systems.

• Design and implement epidemiological modelling frameworks.

• Validate and calibrate models using large-scale national datasets, ensuring scientific robustness, methodological validity, and relevance for policy and decision-making.

• Translate research findings into evidence supporting risk-based disease prevention, preparedness, and control.

• Establish and maintain collaborations with key stakeholders, including the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration, industry partners such as SEGES and Landbrug & Fødevarer (L&F), and international organisations such as the FAO.

• Lead and secure independent research funding through competitive national and international funding calls. The position requires demonstrated experience in securing external funding, as well as the ambition to develop research ideas into externally funded projects and provide scientific leadership for such projects within the TIPTON Research Group.

• Contribute to the development and delivery of One Health and sustainability teaching, with a particular focus on infectious diseases, disease preparedness, and the interactions between animal, human, and environmental health.

• Contribute to teaching in data science, including data management, dataset preparation and handling, statistical analysis, programming, and the analysis of large-scale and complex datasets.

• Supervise students and contribute to research capacity building within infectious disease epidemiology, disease modelling, data science, and One Health.

• Contribute to the delivery of government services undertaken by the Department, including research-based advice, preparedness activities, risk assessments, and other activities relevant to infectious disease modelling and control.

The position is expected to combine methodological excellence in infectious disease modelling and data science with applied epidemiological research, generating evidence that is directly relevant to disease preparedness, private and public bodies, sustainable production systems, animal health and resilient health systems.

The tenure track assistant professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

• research, including publication/academic dissemination

• research-based teaching

• sharing knowledge with society

• participation in formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors

The tenure track assistant professor’s performance will be evaluated through annual evaluations. Furthermore, the tenure track assistant professor will be evaluated in a mid-track appraisal.

After no more than six years of employment and on condition of a positive final appraisal, the tenure track assistant professor will be employed as associate professor. Find more information about tenure track at the University of Copenhagen.

Required qualifications

To be qualified for an assistant professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

• a PhD degree or similar qualifications within the subject area

• research experience within the field of the position

The tenure track assistant professor must have an academic standing showing internationally competitive research, and/or have internationally recognized high potential to make a future impact.

The assistant professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

Salary and employment conditions

The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

The position is permanent.

jobs.occupation: Maternity Cover - Associate Category Manager, Indirect Spend
jobs.description:
Are you a proactive and results-driven professional eager to make a significant impact in the green energy sector? Semco Maritime is offering a unique, temporary opportunity for an Associate Category Manager to join our team for a minimum of 12 months maternity cover.

**Your position

**As an Associate Category Manager for Indirect Spend you will play a pivotal role in leading category strategies across various sectors including facility management, professional services, travel, and more. This role is perfect for someone who thrives in negotiating and driving cost efficiencies while promoting sustainable practices within the supply chain.

At Semco Maritime safety is a core value, and in this role, you will contribute to maintaining and promoting a strong safety culture while delivering innovative solutions. Above all, your work will make a real change for the global energy sector.

Your workplace will be located at our Global Headquarters in Esbjerg, positioned at the heart of the Danish energy industry with stunning waterfront views. This is a full-time, temporary maternity cover for a minimum duration of 12 months.

**Your Tasks & Responsibilities

**As an Associate Category Manager, your primary responsibility will be to support our Group Support Functions, including HR, Marketing and IT, with strategic procurement and day-to-day purchasing activities. You will also manage indirect spend, with particular responsibility for facility management, including Travel.

• Group Support Functions: Partner with functions such as HR, Marketing and IT to understand their requirements and provide procurement support aligned with business needs.

• Contract Negotiation: Lead and support supplier negotiations to achieve competitive pricing and favourable terms and conditions.

• Purchase Order Management: Coordinate and issue purchase orders, follow up on invoice handling and help ensure compliance with the procurement-to-pay process.

• Cost Management: Maintain visibility of expenditure, support budget control and identify opportunities to reduce costs and improve commercial value.

• Indirect Spend and Facility Management: Manage relevant indirect spend categories, including facility management services, and support effective supplier performance and service delivery.

• Group Travel: Manage the travel category across the Semco Group, including supplier relationships, commercial agreements, cost optimisation and stakeholder support.

**Your Profile & Qualifications

**We are looking for an outgoing and positive individual who is passionate about indirect spend and wants to leave their personal mark on it. You have a proactive and organised approach to your work and are eager to enhance your skills within the department.

• Minimum experience of 2 years in Strategic Procurement or a related commercial field, experience in indirect spend is advantageous but not required.

• Excellent negotiation and relationship-building skills, capable of interacting effectively across diverse cultures and functions. Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize effectively.

• Positive, proactive, and a team player with the autonomy to operate independently.

• Fluent in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

**Welcome to Semco Maritime

**At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey. How to get there. By providing the answers needed to make change real. Because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever, pragmatic solutions. This is what we do. This is what we invite you to participate in.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.

So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too.

We know that our people are our greatest strength. We strive to build an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves, contribute their perspectives, and feel part of the team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and believe that diverse teams help us find better solutions and move the energy transition forward.

Care to join the movement?

Change. With us.

At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

**This position reports to:

**Project Operations Manager

__

**Your role and tasks

**We are looking for a Project Manager to lead service, upgrade, retrofit and modification projects within automation and control systems delivered to energy sector process- or offshore industry. In this role, you will take ownership of your own projects and play a key part in ensuring successful delivery for customers within either the energy sector, process- & production industry or to offshore clients (e.g. power plants, district heating facilities, waste incineration plants).

Working closely with customers, engineering teams and experienced project management colleagues, you will be involved throughout the entire project lifecycle, from planning and coordination to execution and completion. This position offers an excellent opportunity to further develop your project management career while gaining exposure to technically advanced solutions, customer collaboration and commercial project execution in an international organization. If you enjoy taking ownership, building relationships and turning plans into successful project deliveries, this could be the ideal next step in your career.

**Your Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Managing service, retrofit and upgrade projects from tender phase through execution and final delivery.

• Leading project planning, scheduling, resource plans and execution activities.

• Building strong customer relationships and acting as a trusted advisor throughout the project lifecycle.

• Managing commercial risks, project changes, claims and recovery actions.

• Project financials steering, including forecasting, cost control and value optimization.

• Identifying & pursuing aftermarket opportunities for upselling.

• Driving contract management and change management activities.

• Ensuring compliance with ABB quality, cybersecurity and HSE requirements.

**Qualifications For The Role

**

• 4–7 years of project management experience within technical, industrial or automation-related environments.

• Proven experience managing project financials, commercial risks and contractual obligations.

• Solid experience leading project teams and driving delivery towards agreed goals and milestones, including experience with remote management.

• Experience working with customers and cross-functional stakeholders in complex project environments.

• Strong understanding of project planning, budgeting and project execution methodologies.

• Experience delivering projects from tender phase through commissioning and handover.

• Knowledge of automation, OT or industrial control systems, preferably within energy, process, power or offshore industries.

• Excellent communication skills in English and experience working with tools such as Azure DevOps, Microsoft Project or similar. PMP, PRINCE2, IPMA or a comparable project management certification is considered an advantage.

**More About Us

**At ABB, we have a clear goal of promoting diversity and inclusion in terms of gender, LGBTQ+, disability, ethnicity, and age. Together, we have embarked on a journey where we all individually and collectively celebrate and welcome individual differences. You can look forward to joining an organization that emphasizes employee well-being. Collaboration and team spirit are key words for us and a crucial foundation for reaching our shared goals. We prioritize a good working environment highly and continuously invest in the education and development of you and your colleagues. If you want to read more about our continuous work with the working environment and sustainability, you can find more information at: https://global.abb/group/en/sustainability

You will be based at one of our offices in Ballerup, Middelfart or Esbjerg, alongside your closest colleagues. In addition, we offer the possibility of working from home a few days a week. Since you support customers across Denmark, you can expect some time on the road, as well as occasional international travel - primarily to the other Nordic countries.

The position reports to Head of Project Management in Service, Nicolai Heilskov.

Apply for the job online via our simple and easily accessible system, where you can also sign up to receive notifications on other opportunities within ABB. If you have questions about the position before then, you are welcome to contact Nicolai Heilskov at +45 21 15 34 38.

The application deadline is 08.11.2026. We look forward to receiving your application.

_ABB is a global technology leader in electrification and automation, enabling a more sustainable future with efficient use of resources. By connecting our knowledge in engineering and digitalization, ABB makes industry more efficient, productive, sustainable, and able to improve their performance. At ABB, we call it 'Engineered to Outrun'. The company has over 140 years of history and more than 110,000 employees worldwide. In Denmark, you will have more than 550 colleagues in offices in Ballerup, Middelfart, Esbjerg, Kalundborg and Aalborg.

_Building a cleaner, smarter future takes all kinds of minds: the curious, the courageous, and the creative. That's why we welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences.

Ready to make an impact?

Apply today or visit https://www.abb.com to learn more about the impact of our solutions across the globe.

Does it excite you to work with cell-based assays to advance innovative peptide-based medicines, and do you have experience with assay automation and liquid handlers? If this sounds like you, and you are ready to take on a broad area of responsibilities, then you could be our new colleague.

**Your new position

**As Senior Laboratory Technician, you will be running cell-based assays to screen and profile candidate drugs in collaboration with other technicians and scientists in the Molecular Pharmacology department. In addition, you will also contribute to the optimization and automation of our laboratory workflows. This role offers a unique opportunity to make a significant contribution to the advancement of our projects by delivering high-quality in vitro data.

**We Offer Exciting Responsibilities

**

• Conducting weekly in vitro assays to assess the efficacy of new peptide drug candidates

• Contributing to the development and improvement of laboratory workflows, with a focus on automation of cell-based assays

• Planning and execution of practical laboratory work

• Processing instrument data in specialized software and databases

• Documentation of laboratory work in the electronic laboratory notebook system

• Responsibilities for maintenance of the lab and lab equipment

• Good collaboration both within and across departments to ensure pace, quality, and exchange of experimental methods and ideas

**Your profile

**You have a mindset aligned with the Zealand values, with curiosity to acquire new skills and learn new methods. You bring a positive attitude and drive, and work both independently and collaboratively. You communicate clearly and have a good understanding of written and spoken English (company language).

**Further, You Have

**

• Education as laboratory technologist, laboratory technician, medical laboratory scientist or similar with at least 3 years of experience with laboratory work

• Proficiency in cell-based assays, including intracellular signaling assays

• Experience with assay automation, including setup and use of liquid handlers

• Hands-on experience with cultivation of mammalian cells

• Strong documentation skills and proficiency with data analysis in Excel, GraphPad Prism or similar software

**Your new team

**You will be part of a department of 17 scientists and 9 technicians dedicated to advancing research and development through generation of in vitro pharmacology and biomarker data, and development of cell-based model systems to deepen understanding of drug mechanism of action. The department is organized into two teams to ensure close managerial support and scientific guidance, and works collaboratively across molecular biology, biochemical, biophysical, and cellular assay platforms to support identification, optimization, and characterization of drug candidates. The position is within our In vitro profiling and signaling team, which focuses on cell-based signaling and binding assays for compound profiling and mechanism-of-action studies.

**Let's bond and be bold

**We have a unique culture, characterized by excellent teamwork and strong engagement across the organization. And we want you to help us strengthen this culture.

Making bonds is at the core of everything we do. From discovering and developing the best new peptide drugs for patients, to engaging with our partners or connecting with each other. We bond through curiosity and playfulness as a team, allowing ourselves to challenge common thinking and drive future innovation. Join us and let's bond and be bold.

Interested in bonding with us? Then please apply no later than November 2nd, 2026, or as soon as possible. The applications will be reviewed as they come in. While a cover letter is not required, please include a few sentences in your CV explaining your motivation for applying.

For further information, please contact Head of In vitro profiling and signaling, Karin Hägerbrand and KHagerbrand@zealandpharma.com.

We are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and welcome applications from all job applicants.

**About Zealand Pharma A/S

**Zealand Pharma A/S (Nasdaq: ZEAL) is a biotechnology company focused on the discovery and development of peptide-based medicines. More than 10 drug candidates invented by Zealand Pharma have advanced into clinical development, of which two have reached the market and three candidates are in late-stage development. The company has development partnerships with a number of pharma companies as well as commercial partnerships for its marketed products. Zealand Pharma was founded in 1998 and is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with a team in the U.S. For more information about Zealand Pharma's business and activities, please visit www.zealandpharma.com.

Are you passionate about building strong quality systems and helping scientific teams deliver reliable, compliant research? Then Minerva Imaging might be your new place of work!

About the job

Minerva Imaging is seeking an experienced and solution-oriented Quality Assurance Manager to lead and continuously improve the Quality Management System for our Contract Research Organization activities. As a non-GLP CRO, we believe quality should support the business and our clients.

As Quality Assurance Manager, you will serve as an independent quality function and collaborate closely with the Quality Working Group and teams across the organization. You will bring a pragmatic, risk-based approach to quality, challenging existing processes where appropriate and developing solutions that are effective, proportionate, and workable in practice.

About the role

You will own the CRO Quality Management System and ensure that studies and supporting activities are conducted in accordance with company procedures, client requirements, applicable regulations, and recognized quality standards. The role combines strategic development of the quality framework with hands-on management of audits, deviations, CAPAs, document control, training, supplier quality, and study quality oversight.

This position is ideal for someone who is comfortable working independently, enjoys extensive stakeholder management, and can translate quality requirements into clear and effective processes in a dynamic CRO environment. Our quality system is evolving, and we are looking for a pragmatic QA leader who thrives in building quality systems that are both effective and workable. You will be comfortable applying risk-based thinking, focusing effort where it creates the greatest value, and helping the organization strengthen compliance without slowing scientific progress.

The position

As Quality Assurance Manager, you will:

• Own and continuously improve Minerva Imaging's CRO Quality Management System, ensuring practical and risk-based compliance.

• Collaborate with the Quality Group and operational teams to maintain high-quality documentation, effective deviation management, and risk-based decision-making across the organization.

• Lead audits, inspections, deviations, CAPAs, and supplier quality activities while maintaining inspection readiness.

• Educate and coach colleagues across the organization to strengthen quality awareness and ownership.

• Serve as the primary quality partner for clients, management, and operational teams, translating quality requirements into fit-for-purpose solutions that support scientific excellence and business objectives.

What will make you successful

You are a collaborative and pragmatic quality professional who:

• Have a strong understanding of Quality Management Systems and apply quality principles with a pragmatic, risk-based mindset.

• Combine auditing, problem-solving, and root cause investigation skills with a focus on practical solutions.

• Work independently, take ownership, and build strong relationships across scientific, operational, and management teams.

• Can influence stakeholders, navigate competing priorities, and translate quality requirements into clear and workable processes.

• Balance structure and compliance with sound judgement, focusing efforts where they create the greatest value.

• Communicate confidently in English and actively promote a culture of quality, learning, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

• A degree in life sciences, veterinary medicine, pharmacy, biomedical sciences, biotechnology, quality management, or a related field.

• Experience from a CRO, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or research environment.

• Demonstrated experience with quality systems, audits, deviations, CAPAs, root cause investigations, and regulatory compliance.

• Experience implementing or maintaining electronic quality systems is preferred.

• Experience supporting client audits and inspections is highly desirable.

• Formal training in Quality Assurance or Quality Management is preferred.

• Excellent organizational, project management, and stakeholder communication skills.

Minerva offers:

We believe in creating an agile working environment, so we have flexible working options including the option of working from home. We care about our employees’ well-being and offer health insurance and a quality conscious lunch scheme and monthly social activities.

We are an informal organization with a strong focus on open and honest communication. We value humour and a natural care for one another.

Application:

Please submit your application to us no later than 08.11.2026. The application must include a motivated cover letter and a CV addressing the listed qualifications. Applications will be evaluated continuously.

If you have questions regarding the position, please contact Kujtim Rexha, HR Business Partner at kur@minervaimaging.com

About Minerva Imaging:

Minerva Imaging is a scientifically driven and fully integrated Contract Research Organization (CRO) and Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) specializing in targeted radionuclide therapies.

We support translational research and drug development through the use of advanced preclinical animal models within oncology and cardiovascular diseases, combined with state-of-the-art in vivo molecular imaging. By working in close partnership with our sponsors, we seek to understand their scientific challenges and jointly identify how our expertise, technologies, and methods can deliver robust and meaningful answers.

Our modern facility in Ølstykke, Denmark offers best-in-class, fully integrated radiopharmaceutical research, development, and manufacturing capabilities - covering the entire value chain from early research to clinical supply.

Backed by Nordic Capital since 2026, Minerva Imaging is executing an ambitious growth strategy aimed at strengthening our position as a market leader within targeted radionuclide therapies. This growth journey offers exciting opportunities for individuals who want to contribute to cutting-edge science in a dynamic and international environment.

Minerva Imaging is an equal opportunity employer, and we welcome applications from qualified candidates regardless of background or experience. In accordance with our recruitment policy, all candidates are required to provide a personal criminal record as part of the hiring process.

Follow us on LinkedIn for the latest news updates or visit www.minervaimaging.com for more information.

Finance & Operations Manager

Full-time | On-site in Søborg/Copenhagen | Visibuilt

Join Visibuilt as we take a fossil-free, fermentation-based binder from the lab to the market. We are looking for an experienced financial controller who would like to be the person keeping a growing climate-tech company financially sound, investor-ready and well organised – from the month-end close to the board pack.

Location: Søborg, Greater Copenhagen (on-site)

Start: 1 January 2027 (or as soon as possible)

Type: Full-time employment

Salary: Competitive and in line with the market, reflecting your experience and responsibilities

Reports to: CEO & Founder, Line Kloster Pedersen

Core focus: Financial control and reporting, operations, grants, board and shareholder administration, financial modelling and fundraising support

About Visibuilt

Visibuilt is building fossil-free alternatives for pavement materials. Our core technology, visiBINDER, is a 100% bio-based binder developed from mycelium and designed to reduce energy use and CO2 emissions in infrastructure materials. We are based at Alfa Laval Innovation House in Søborg, just outside Copenhagen.

The role

Visibuilt has grown from an early-stage startup into a company with institutional investors, an active board, several public grant projects and an R&D team whose decisions need solid numbers behind them. You will be our finance and administration function: the person who makes sure our numbers are accurate, on time and useful for decisions – and who owns the operational backbone of the company.

·       A broad role with real ownership. You will be our only finance person, so you plan and manage your own areas – including the operational processes that keep a growing team running – in close collaboration with the CEO, our CTO, our external accountant and payroll administration, auditors and lawyers.

·       Cash is king.  You will own the cashflow budget and rolling forecast, so we always know our runway and spot pinch points well before they arrive. With several grant projects running, customer project, and heavy R&D, this means keeping a close eye on when money actually lands compared with when we spend it.

·       You oversee the bookkeeping. Our external accountant handles the day-to-day entries. Your job is to monitor, quality-check and follow up on their work, and to turn it into reporting the CEO and board can rely on.

·       Real business impact. You get to understand our business and provide market analyses for business development and cost models for R&D.

Responsibilities

Financial control

·       Monitor and quality-check invoicing, payroll and bookkeeping carried out by our external accountant (e-conomic) and approve payments together with management.

Reporting, audit & annual accounts

·       Deliver monthly finance reporting, budget-vs-actual and runway forecasts for management and the board.

·       Take responsibility for the annual accounts and the audit process with our auditors, meeting investor deadlines.

Operations ownership

·       Look after our people operations: keep the employee handbook and policies up to date, and run holiday planning and time registration.

Grant management

·       Manage our public grant portfolio (e.g. EUDP): project budgets, timesheets, reimbursement claims and progress reporting.

·       Support new grant applications with budgets and co-financing plans.

Board, shareholders & governance

·       Act as board secretary: prepare board packs, take minutes and follow up on decisions.

·       Manage shareholder matters – shareholder register, warrant programmes, general meetings, investor reporting and filings with the Danish Business Authority – with support from our lawyers. You coordinate and execute a quarterly shareholder report with the CEO.

Support for business development and R&D

·       Build market analyses (market sizing, segments, pricing) that support the CEO’s commercial work.

·       Build cost models together with R&D and production, so technical choices are informed by unit economics.

Fundraising

·       Be responsible for the financial projections and scenario models used in fundraising and investor dialogues.

·       Maintain our data room and coordinate due diligence processes.

What we are looking for

·       Solid experience in finance – typically 8 years or more – including time as financial controller, finance manager or similar. Experience from audit also counts.

·       Experience with the full finance cycle: month-end close, management reporting, annual accounts and working with auditors.

·       Experience reviewing the work of an external accounting partner.

·       Strong Excel skills: you are comfortable building budgets, forecasts and cost models from scratch.

·       You can explain financial analysis clearly to non-finance colleagues, and you are open about your assumptions.

·       Professional English is required; Danish is strongly preferred.

Nice to have

·       Experience from a start-up, scale-up or SME where you covered a broad range of tasks.

·       Experience managing and reporting on public grants (e.g. Innovation Fund Denmark, EUDP, MUDP or Horizon Europe), including timesheets and reimbursement claims.

·       Fundraising experience: data rooms, due diligence and investor financial models.

·       Board secretary work, shareholder registers, general meetings and company filings.

·       Background from manufacturing, materials or construction – helpful for unit-cost models.

·       Comfortable using AI and automation to speed up routine finance work.

How you work

·       Reliable. You are on time and prepared – especially with investors, auditors and other external partners.

·       You follow through. You see tasks through to completion, and ask for input along the way when you need it.

·       You share your view openly. You raise questions and concerns in the room, and once a decision is made you support it fully.

·       You work in shared systems. Everything lives in the company’s systems and shared drive and you have an eye for making systems more efficient to save time.

·       You use AI with care. For speed – never as a replacement for analysis you have checked yourself.

What success looks like

·       Monthly reporting is delivered on time and of high quality.

·       The annual accounts and audit are completed on time and without surprises.

·       Grant reimbursements and reports are submitted on time, with no rework.

·       Our financial and cost models are up to date and actively used in R&D, business development and fundraising decisions.

·       The data room is kept due-diligence ready, and our operational processes simply work.

What you can expect from Visibuilt

Visibuilt offers the chance to shape the finance and operations of a climate-tech company at a defining stage, in a small, committed team where your work has direct impact.

·       A key role close to the CEO and the board, with real influence on how Visibuilt is run and scaled.

·       An attractive salary package incl. pension, and participation in our healthcare program.

·       A mission-driven company building bio-based alternatives for construction materials.

·       On-site collaboration in Søborg at Alfa Laval Innovation House.

·       Flexible working hours, so you can plan your work around the rest of your life.

·       Participation in our warrant program and 30 days of paid holiday each year.

Not ticking every box?

Many candidates only apply when they meet every single requirement.

If you recognise yourself in most of this role but not all of it, we would still very much like to hear from you.

Application process

Please apply by 6 November 2026 by emailing your CV (PDF) to job@visibuilt.dk with the subject line “Finance & Operations Manager – [your name]”. We review applications and hold first interviews on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply early. Interviews will take place between 9 and 20 November.

A cover letter is not required. Instead, please answer these five questions briefly in your email:

• 
 Are you legally authorized to work in Denmark?

• 
 Have you been responsible for month-end close, management reporting and annual accounts, including the auditor process?

• 
 Have you reviewed and quality-checked the work of an external accounting partner?

• 
 What is your notice period?

• 
 What is your level of Danish (none / basic / professional / native)?

We aim to keep the recruitment process fair and unbiased, so please do not include a photo in your CV.

We use AI tools to assist in the initial review of applications; all decisions are made by people.

Today we are 12 people with very different backgrounds, and we would like even more diversity – so whoever you are, we would love to hear from you.

Questions about the position? Please contact Line Kloster Pedersen, CEO, at line@visibuilt.dk, and put job@visibuilt.dk in copy. You are also welcome to call our chairman, Kresten Kloch, on +45 42 82 82 12

Practical note

We would like our new colleague to start on 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible.
